title: The global search PR queried MailAccount and MailRule with plain .objects.filter() behind only a model-level has_perm check, unlike the owner-aware get_objects_for_user_owner_aware() it used for tags and correspondents, so users see other users' mail accounts and rules.

vulnerable_findings.explanation: SearchResultSerializer.to_representation fetches a Document by a user‑controlled identifier (instance["id"]) using Document.objects.get without any permission check, potentially allowing an IDOR where a user could obtain data for a document they are not authorized to view if the serializer is invoked with unfiltered input.

def to_representation(self, instance):
    doc = (
        Document.objects.select_related(
            "correspondent",
            "storage_path",
            "document_type",
            "owner",
        )
        .prefetch_related("tags", "custom_fields", "notes")
        .get(id=instance["id"])
    )
    notes = ",".join([
        str(c.note) for c in doc.notes.all()],
    )
    r = super().to_representation(doc)
    r["__search_hit__"] = {
        "score": instance.score,
        "highlights": instance.highlights("content", text=doc.content),
        "note_highlights": (instance.highlights("notes", text=notes) if doc else None),
        "rank": instance.rank,
    }
    return r

All objects (documents, tags, etc.) allow setting object‑level permissions with optional `owner` and / or a `set_permissions` parameters ... assuming the authenticated user has permission to do so (the user must be the object owner or a superuser).

findings.suggested_fix: Before fetching the Document, verify that the requesting user has the required object‑level permission (e.g., using get_objects_for_user_owner_aware or checking doc.owner / permissions). Alternatively, pass the already permission‑filtered Document instance from the view instead of re‑querying by ID.

: Allows authentication via HTTP_REMOTE_USER which is used by some SSO

    !!! warning

        This will allow authentication by simply adding a

        especially *must* ensure that any such header is not passed from

        effectively bypass all authentication).

        If you're exposing paperless to the internet directly (i.e.
